newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen nearing decision on E-Plus stake.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen nearing decision on E-Plus stake.

text.p: German industrial group Thyssen AG said on Friday it was nearing a decision on whether to sell its 30.1 percent stake in the E-Plus mobil phone network.
Thyssen said it hired investment bank SBC Warburg to plan the future development of its share and that a sale was one possibility.
The steel and engineering group could also push E-Plus to expand into fixed-line teleocmmunications, a spokeswoman said.
Veba AG, which itself owns 30.1 percent of E-Plus, has expressed interest in buying Thyssen's share, but has so far balked at Thyssen's asking price of 3.5 billion marks.

BellSouth Corp. owns 22 percent of E-Plus. The network expected to double sales in 1997 to to about 500 million marks, but trails well behind the two top mobile phone service providers -- Deutsche Telekom AG and Mannesmann AG.
